cards.ja: 今日の朝ごはんは、わたしのおごりです。
いいえ、本当に、わたしに払わせてください。

cards.en: OK, thanks, but next time it's on me.
cards.ja: じゃあ、ありがとうございます。でも次は、わたしがおごります。
cards.glossEn: OK, thanks, but next time it's on me.

cards.ja: それなら、わたしがチップを置きます。

cards.en: Is it customary to leave a tip here?
cards.ja: ここでは、チップを置く習慣がありますか？
cards.glossEn: Is it customary to leave a tip here?

cards.en: Shall we split the bill among all of us?
cards.ja: 会計はみんなで割り勘にしましょうか？
cards.glossEn: Shall we split the bill among all of us?

reader.en: After a breakfast of coffee and sweet bread in Oaxaca, the waiter brings the bill to our table.
reader.ja: オアハカで、コーヒーと菓子パンの朝ごはんを食べたあと、ウェイターがわたしたちのテーブルに伝票を持ってきます。
reader.glossEn: After a breakfast of coffee and sweet bread in Oaxaca, the waiter brings the bill to our table.

reader.en: I take out my card and say: Breakfast is on me today, because you showed me the city.
reader.ja: わたしはカードを取り出して言います。「今日の朝ごはんは、わたしのおごりです。ふたりがこの街を案内してくれたから。」
reader.glossEn: I take out my card and say: Breakfast is on me today, because you showed me the city.

reader.en: My new friends, Lucía and Andrés, insist: No, here you are our guest.
reader.ja: 新しい友達のルシアとアンドレスは、こう言ってゆずりません。「いいえ、ここではあなたがわたしたちのゲストです。」
reader.glossEn: My new friends, Lucía and Andrés, insist: No, here you are our guest.

reader.en: I tell them: No, really, let me pay, but Andrés is already giving cash to the waiter.
reader.ja: 「いいえ、本当に、わたしに払わせてください」とふたりに言いますが、アンドレスはもうウェイターに現金を渡しています。
reader.glossEn: I tell them: No, really, let me pay, but Andrés is already giving cash to the waiter.

reader.en: So I ask: Is it customary to leave a tip here?
reader.ja: そこで、わたしはたずねます。「ここでは、チップを置く習慣がありますか？」
reader.glossEn: So I ask: Is it customary to leave a tip here?

reader.en: Lucía says that they usually leave 10 percent if the service is good.
reader.ja: ルシアは、サービスがよければ、自分たちはふだん10パーセントのチップを置くと言います。
reader.glossEn: Lucía says that they usually leave 10 percent if the service is good.

reader.en: I tell them: If you pay the bill, then I'll leave the tip, and they agree.
reader.ja: 「ふたりがお会計をするなら、わたしがチップを置きます」と言うと、ふたりはそれを受け入れます。
reader.glossEn: I tell them: If you pay the bill, then I'll leave the tip, and they agree.

reader.en: At the end I say: OK, thanks, but next time it's on me, and everyone laughs.
reader.ja: 最後に、わたしは言います。「じゃあ、ありがとうございます。でも次は、わたしがおごります。」そして、みんなが笑います。
reader.glossEn: At the end I say: OK, thanks, but next time it's on me, and everyone laughs.

issues: The source reports Lucía and Andrés usually leave a 10 percent tip if service is good; this is their stated practice, not an asserted Oaxaca-wide rule.
The waiter brings a table bill/伝票, while the bill-to-pay card uses お会計. Qualified Japanese/dictionary review should settle these contextual senses.

The source guest/invitado is rendered ゲスト, distinct from a café customer. Friends use tú in Spanish; the Japanese deliberately keeps polite learner-facing dialogue and あなた, pending naturalness review.
Pan dulce/sweet bread is rendered 菓子パン without naming a specific Mexican item; qualified food and Japanese review remains open.
Oaxaca, Lucía and Andrés katakana and café waiter terminology require locale/name/register review.
The card payment is only offered, never completed; Andrés is already handing cash to the waiter, with no amount or change added.
The 10 percent figure, if-service-is-good condition, narrator tip offer and next-time treat remain source reported and need contextual dictionary/speaking review.
The archive introduces register-vs-table and ask-staff dialogue absent from current source; no archive row or audio/progress position is imported.
